Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have internal alignment to move forward with a staged EU residency rollout: Phase 1 (Ireland pilot, Q3), Phase 2 (Spain + NL, Q4), Phase 3 (full EU GA, Q1 next year).

A few procurement questions we need clarity on before the pilot PO:
- How do you typically structure credits for compliance add-ons across a staged rollout? We want to avoid paying full HSM seats up front if we only need 1 seat for pilot.
- Can audit-log retention be purchased as a pilot-tier (shorter retention) and converted to GA retention with crediting for the initial pilot delta?
- How do you treat KMS/HSM seat pricing vs per-token/per-GB metrics for pilot vs committed volumes?

Attached is our audit scope doc (audit_scope.xlsx) which gives rough retention needs for the pilot. Happy to do a 30m sync — Samir and I can be available Mon/Tue next week.

Two immediate asks:
1) A short note on amortization/crediting options you can offer for pilot -> GA (prefer a concrete framework we can show finance).
2) Any quick ballpark on HSM seat min-term and pilot discount ranges.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Director, Cloud Procurement
Lifecare Health

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment, very helpful. High level responses below; we can put numbers to this after a quick internal cost review and a short call.

1) Pilot crediting framework (recommended):
   - We hold back a small, refundable pilot credit pool (e.g., 30–40% of the expected first-year add-on value). This pool covers audit-log overages and one-time HSM seat setup during pilot.
   - If customer commits to a 12-month EU residency contract at GA, the pilot pool is applied pro-rata to the committed add-on spend (i.e., not duplicated). If they do not commit, the pool is credited against final pilot usage invoice (less provisioning/setup fees).

2) Audit logs: pilot-tier retention (30 days) billed at a promo rate; transition to GA (90+ days) triggers a one-time conversion that calculates the delta and consumes the pilot credit pool first.

3) KMS/HSM seats:
   - HSM: recommend 1 seat for pilot (reduced install/setup fee) with option to scale. Seat pricing is typically a combination of a small monthly seat fee + ephemeral setup charge. We can offer a pilot discounted seat fee (20–40%) and then a seat-credit to be applied at GA if they commit.
   - KMS (software-managed): priced per-tenant with negligible setup; conversion to GA is typically a straight application of credits.

Ive looped in Olga for cost-model detail and Monica for sales/crediting language. Proposed next steps:
- Internal: Olga to share a quick cost model (examples: per-seat math + retention band pricing).
- Sales: Monica to draft a short crediting clause we can include in the SOW/PO.
- Joint call: 30m next Tue at 10am CET (let me know if that works).

Quick note: from a compliance POV there are some non-negotiable items (HSM physical residency, key export controls) which may affect seat counts and provisioning windows — Olga will spell this out.

Thanks,

Rishi / Samir — I looked through the audit scope and sketched two concrete cost approaches (attached: cost_model_v1.csv):

Option A — Seat-first (lower variable spend)
- HSM: monthly seat fee = €3,200 (pilot discount 30% → €2,240); one-time provisioning = €4,500 (reduced for pilot).
- Audit logs: tiered by retention band. Pilot (30 days) = €0.60/GB/month; GA (90 days) = €1.50/GB/month. Conversion delta consumes credits.

Option B — Usage-first (lower upfront)
- HSM: minimal pilot seat fee (€900/mo) + higher setup amortized over 6 months. GA conversion triggers a true-up where a credit is applied against the remaining setup balance.
- Audit logs: priced per-GB with volume breakpoints; GA rates offer ~30% lower per-GB if committed volume thresholds met.

Observations:
- For a staged rollout where Phase 1 is small, Option B reduces cash outlay for Lifecare. If Lifecare is comfortable with a 12-month commit for Phase 3, we can move to Option A at GA and apply pilot credits.
- We should confirm the expected ingest for Phase 1 (Samir: the audit_scope has ranges but a midpoint would help).

I attached the CSV with worked examples and a simple amortization column for converting pilot discounts to GA credits.

Olga Petrov
Senior Compliance PM, Redwood Inference

- We can offer a pilot package that combines: 1 HSM pilot seat (discounted 35%), audit-log pilot retention at promo rates for up to 90 days, and a one-time professional services credit of €2,000 to help with onboarding.
